hypothesis: Near-unit binomial correction computes the same unique real polar map as an independent high-precision spectral construction, while avoiding reconstruction of identity from near-degenerate eigenvectors.

fixed_conditions.input: dense QR isometry plus explicit same-space tangent or symmetric normal perturbations; float64 coordinates
fixed_conditions.oracle: mpmath 75-decimal complete Gram eigenproblem/inverse square root
fixed_conditions.physics_scope: no Hamiltonian, no-pair projector, core freezing, CI ensemble, residual metric or convergence threshold changes

controls: Gram infinity norm just below and above the 0.01 branch threshold
right orthogonal rotation and column phase flip
the public optimizer seed still uses its original separate spectral polar construction

gates.seed_initialization: original gram eigensolve block remains; helper called only by trial retract

stopping_condition: one fixed matrix panel; no scan or orbitals optimization rerun
limits: Same mathematical map and floating-point arithmetic check, not evidence of Yb stationarity or of a physical-energy error bound. A speedup is not measured.
